messages:
alex: FYI perf-alert: p99 latency for attention kernel after yesterday's kernel-selector change jumped ~18% on prod-smoketest. attaching quick numbers below.

 tara: ugh. which kernel variant + which workload?

 alex: Kernel group = attn-opt-v2 (fused->fallback path when seq>1024). Workload = chat-high-latency profile (median seq ~600, tail ~1400). perf-bot triggered on 5 of 8 benchmarks.

 ravi: do we have raw histograms? could be sample bias from small sample size at tail.

 alex: pasted compressed hist snippets from perf harness:
 ```
 name: chat-high-latency
 p50: 42ms -> 44ms
 p95: 120ms -> 130ms
 p99: 240ms -> 283ms
 samples: 1200 -> 1280
 config: batch=8, kv_cache=true, quant=fp16
 commit: 9f3a7d1 (kernel-selector tweak)
 ```

 lee: interesting that samples increased. suggests more heavy tails, not fewer samples. did kernel-selection change the routing rule (seq threshold) or the fallback cost calc?

 alex: it tightened the fallback cost calc. hypoth: the new cost model favors fallback for borderline seqs causing more context-switches and worse micro-batching.

 tara: can we repro locally with the harness using same sequence length mix? add deterministic rng seed and warmup iterations.

 ravi: +1. also run with and without kv_cache warmup to see cache-warm penalty. add a flag --no-warmup to isolate.

 perf-bot: perf check completed: see https://perf.redwood/ci/1823456789 (summary: regression confirmed on p99 for attn-opt-v2 on chat-high-latency).

 alex: quick repro plan I'm going to run: 1) reproduce harness with seed=42 and seq-distribution from production logs, 2) toggle fallback threshold from 1024->1152, 3) collect kernel-level counters (context-switches, micro-batch sizes).

 lee: also capture torch/cu context switch stats and queue wait time. sometimes GPU kernel launch pattern is the root.

 tara: while alex runs repro, I'll bisect the selector change set to find the exact line. if we find a single bad heuristic we can revert.

 ravi: for triage criteria: if p99 regression >10% and throughput drop >5% across 3 runs (seeded) mark as severity-high and revert canary.

 alex: first repro run logs (seeded):
 ```
 [run1] p99=279ms, throughput=92 tokens/s
 counters: micro_batches: 24->38, avg_batch=3.1
 kv_warm=enabled, cache_miss_first=0.42
 ```

 alex: second run with fallback threshold bumped to 1152:
 ```
 [run2] p99=241ms, throughput=98 tokens/s
 micro_batches: 20, avg_batch=4.0
 ```

 tara: that delta looks like selector is misrouting borderline sequences into a slower fallback. nice repro.

 lee: action items:
 - alex: open a rollback PR to revert the heuristic change and add unit tests for fallback decision (deadline EOD).
 - tara: add integration test in smokebench that covers seq-distribution with synthetic tail.
 - ravi: run a 10-run seeded sweep to quantify variance and update triage doc thresholds.
 - infra: add a perf-bot alert annotation to include avg_batch and micro_batch_count.

 alex: opened PR #4123 to revert + test. description references commit 9f3a7d1 and includes a small perf unit that asserts avg_batch >= 3.5 in the smoketest.

 perf-bot: CI note: PR #4123 triggered smokebench; current run shows p99 back to 242ms.

 tara: nice. follow-up: we still want the original intent of the heuristic (avoid slow fused kernel for long seqs). proposal: instead of hard threshold, use model-predicted runtime delta (cheap model) + batch-size penalty. put in RFC follow-up.

 ravi: also add correctness checks: token-by-token random-match for 5 sequences across kernels to ensure no silent numerical drift when switching paths.

 alex: noted. I put a TODO in PR and linked this thread. will coordinate RFC draft tomorrow.

 lee: thanks everyone. triage complete for now. rolling back on canary and will monitor next 24h. :white_check_mark:

 alex: thanks — will post bench artifacts to the perf dashboard and follow up with RFC ticket number. @perf-bot please keep this thread pinned to the rollback PR.

 ci-bot: Per request, pinned link to PR #4123 and perf run 1823456899.

 ravi: one last note — add a small doc in eng-runtime/bench-guides about seeding and sample sizes; we keep tripping on noisy tail signals.

 tara: agreed. I'll start a PR for bench-guides after lunch. :coffee:
